name: dsh-vim
description: Vim-style keyboard scrolling (d = down, e = up) for whichever pane the pointer is over — the conversation or the sidebar — a message box that never takes focus on its own (space puts the caret in it, and takes it back out while the box is empty), a choice of what a bare Enter does in the composer (sends, breaks the line, does nothing, or sends on a double Enter — Ctrl/Cmd+Enter always sends, and the composer's own dock row says which), a reasoning-level stepper (q), a model picker (w) that opens a small window listing your chosen models with every reasoning level each one publishes beside it — d / e to move between models, Tab to move between levels, w again to switch, Escape to cancel — plus a task window (f) that answers what is waiting on you before where things live: a block for everything whose ball is in your court (an approval, a plan review, a question, or a run you have not looked at yet) ordered longest-waiting first, a dimmed block for turns in flight, then the last three hours in plain time order (measured across the whole pool, so a run in flight still counts as activity; when the window is genuinely empty the block says Earlier rather than Recent and falls back to the newest batch) — a folder is a label on each row rather than a container around rows, so a busy folder can no longer starve a quiet one out of the list; the attention blocks are read off the whole pool so a debt older than the recency window cannot hide behind the More seat, each row is listed once, and the headline says so in words when nothing needs you; the window opens on the first thing waiting on you so dealing with one row makes the next press land on the next, a running turn's clock counts in whole minutes and stays quiet under the first one, each row leads with its state chip and then the folder and name, so the eye reads what it is doing before it reads which conversation, the just-finished chip pulses once when the window opens so the eye lands on it, and the More seat can be walked onto and confirmed with d / e and the open key — a click outside either window closes it, Escape still does, and the click itself still reaches the page, and on the board every card leads its meta line with the same state chip the task window's rows carry (waiting on you outranks running, which outranks just finished), so the board answers what each conversation is doing as well as where it lives; the board is also a sidebar page beside Plugins and Automation, drawn as a canvas: one panel per workspace in play today, its conversations stacked under it, and the inbox as a panel of its own; panels are dragged by their headings, bare paper is dragged to pan the canvas, tidy lays the panels back on a grid, a fork is drawn as an indented child under its parent with a line joining them when this client watched the fork (ordinary forks carry no durable parent in the session log, so older branches are shown as roots rather than guessed), entering happens only through each card's Enter button while pressing the card's name renames it in place instead of navigating, and loose text cards can be written anywhere on the canvas, dragged freely and deleted; a card dropped on a conversation is tied to it by a measured line and snapped into the margin beside its panel, while a card dropped on that conversation's Enter button opens it and pastes the card's words into the composer as a draft (never sending) and stays behind as a greyed, dashed-line trace marked done; the running chip carries its own clock, ticking in place once a minute, and a status tick that changes no card's word costs no repaint; and notes are written on the board itself: a card's note mark opens a field inside the card, Enter keeps the line, Escape drops it, and a press elsewhere keeps it too; pressing the line again edits it and emptying it takes it away, while the note key (n) opens the board on the conversation on screen with that card's field already waiting — the lines are stored apart from the board's own arrangement, so a board reset cannot cost the reader a thought
